mainTopic: When an idol becomes forbidden according to רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא, how each uses the פסוקים, and questions about the impurity of idol vessels and offerings.
overview: The גמרא finishes רבי ישמעאל's reading of דברים 12:2. A נכרי's idol is forbidden only once it is worshipped, learned by a היקש to כלים. A Jew's idol is forbidden immediately. רבי ישמעאל's source for the Jew's idol is tested step by step: first סברא, then the עגל, then ארור. It is finally proven from 'תועבת ה׳'. רבי עקיבא holds the reverse: a נכרי's idol is forbidden once carved (פסילי אלהיהם), and a Jew's idol only once worshipped (ושם בסתר). The גמרא then shows how each תנא uses the other's פסוקים for other teachings: ביטול by a נכרי, גניזה of a Jew's idol, and ריש לקיש's lesson about appointing an unfit judge. Next, רב המנונא asks about a welded vessel used for an idol. This becomes a double question about whether old rabbinic impurity, and especially idol impurity, returns to a remade vessel, and it ends in תיקו. Finally, רבי יוחנן asks רבי ינאי whether ביטול purifies food offered to an idol. The גמרא explains why he did not ask about vessels or the idol itself, and that explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Applying the verse to vessels, and the rule about idols
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק cannot be about the places themselves, so it is applied to כלים. From here comes the rule: a נכרי's idol is forbidden only once worshipped, and a Jew's idol is forbidden immediately.
steps.simpleTranslation: Apply the verse to vessels. From here the Sages said: a non-Jew's idol is not forbidden until it is worshipped, but a Jew's idol is forbidden immediately.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבי ישמעאל's reading of the פסוק and states the rule that comes out of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The places where idols were served are not forbidden, so the words 'אשר עבדו שם' are moved over to כלים used in worship. Those כלים become forbidden only once they are actually used. The rule given here goes further and also covers the idol itself: a נכרי's idol waits for worship, but a Jew's does not.

keyTerms.meaning: Apply it to another topic. Used when a פסוק cannot mean its plain topic, so it is moved to a related one.
Vessels or utensils, here ones used to serve an idol

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic rule that the rest of this section tries to explain and prove.

phrases.english: Apply it to the matter of vessels.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the פסוק 'אשר עבדו שם' (דברים 12:2). It can't mean the places themselves, so we use it for vessels instead.

phrases.english: From here they said:
A non-Jew's idol
is not forbidden until it is worshipped,
and a Jew's is forbidden immediately.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי ישמעאל's reading of the פסוק, which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נכרי's idol is forbidden only once worshipped. A Jew's idol is forbidden immediately.

steps.title: But the verse was applied to vessels, not to idols
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: we just said the פסוק is about כלים, so how can it teach a rule about the idol itself?
steps.simpleTranslation: But we explained this verse as talking about vessels!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges Step 1. If the פסוק was moved over to כלים, it should not teach anything about idols.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 moved the פסוק to the topic of כלים, but then stated a rule about the idol itself. These seem to be two different topics. The question is how the rule crosses from vessels to idols.

keyTerms.meaning: We established it as, or we explained it as referring to

phrases.english: But we established it as being about vessels!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the jump from vessels to idols in Step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule about idols in Step 1
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק that was moved to כלים cannot also teach about the idols themselves.

steps.title: The verse compares their gods to the vessels
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק places 'their gods' right next to the vessels. That is a היקש: just as כלים are forbidden only after use, so are idols.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'that you are dispossessing them, their gods.' It compares 'their gods' to the vessels. Just as vessels are forbidden only once they are used for worship, so too their gods are forbidden only once they are worshipped.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק itself links idols to כלים, so the vessel rule carries over to the idols.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because 'אלהיהם' appears in the same phrase as the vessels, the פסוק teaches by היקש that they share a law. כלים need actual worship before they become forbidden, so a נכרי's idol also needs actual worship.

keyTerms.meaning: Compares, making a היקש between two things in a פסוק

phrases.english: The verse says:
"That you are dispossessing them, their gods,"
phrases.notes: דברים 12:2

phrases.english: it compares "their gods" to vessels.

so too their gods are forbidden only once they are worshipped.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: היקש from the wording of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק speaks only about כלים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק links idols to כלים, so a נכרי's idol is forbidden only once worshipped.

steps.title: Why רבי עקיבא does not make this comparison
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא does not accept this היקש. He holds that the word 'את' separates 'their gods' from the vessels.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא, who does not make this comparison, would tell you: the word 'את' breaks off the topic.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי עקיבא would read the same פסוק without the comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי ישמעאל, the words sit together and are compared. רבי עקיבא sees the word 'את' before 'אלהיהם' as a divider that starts a new topic. So he does not learn the idol rule from the כלים.

keyTerms.meaning: He would say to you. Gives the other opinion's reply.
Interrupted the topic, separating it from what came before

phrases.english: And רבי עקיבא, who does not make this comparison,
would say to you:
The word "את" breaks off the topic.
phrases.notes: He means the little word את right before אלהיהם in the פסוק.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא דְּלָא מַקֵּישׁ, אָמַר לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view on the היקש from Step 3.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי עקיבא holds that 'את' separates the topics, so there is no היקש.

steps.title: Where does רבי ישמעאל learn that a Jew's idol is forbidden immediately?
steps.stepSummary: The היקש only proves the rule for a נכרי's idol. What is the source for a Jew's idol being forbidden right away?
steps.simpleTranslation: And as for רבי ישמעאל: we found that a non-Jew's idol is not forbidden until it is worshipped. From where does he know that a Jew's idol is forbidden immediately?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that the second half of the rule in Step 1 still has no source, and asks for one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The היקש covered only 'אלהיהם', meaning the idols of the nations. Nothing so far has taught anything about a Jew's idol. The rest of this section is the search for that source.

keyTerms.meaning: We have found a source for
From where does he know it?

phrases.english: And as for רבי ישמעאל,

steps.title: It comes from logic
steps.stepSummary: It is a סברא. Since a נכרי's idol needs worship, a Jew's idol must be different and be forbidden right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is logic: since a non-Jew's idol is forbidden only once worshipped, a Jew's is forbidden immediately.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that no פסוק is needed, because the rule follows from logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that the Torah singled out the נכרי's idol for the 'wait until worship' rule. That suggests a Jew's idol is the opposite and is forbidden at once. The next steps test whether this logic really holds.

keyTerms.meaning: Logical reasoning, as opposed to a source from a פסוק

phrases.english: It is logic:
since a non-Jew's idol is forbidden only once it is worshipped,
a Jew's is forbidden immediately.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It follows logically from the contrast with a נכרי's idol.

steps.title: Maybe a Jew's idol is not forbidden at all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the logic. Why not say the opposite extreme, that a Jew's idol is never forbidden?
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: a Jew's idol is not forbidden at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on Step 6. The contrast could just as easily point to 'never forbidden' as to 'forbidden immediately'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the only point is that a Jew's idol differs from a נכרי's, the difference could go in either direction. Since the Torah spoke only about the nations' idols, maybe a Jew's idol is not covered by the איסור at all.

phrases.english: Say instead: a Jew's is not forbidden at all!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the logic of Step 6.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The contrast with a נכרי's idol could equally mean that a Jew's idol is never forbidden.

steps.title: An idol that must be buried must also be forbidden
steps.stepSummary: A Jew's idol has to be put away in גניזה. It cannot be that something needing גניזה is not forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, it requires burial, and it would not become forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the 'not forbidden at all' idea by pointing to the known rule that a Jew's idol needs גניזה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A Jew's idol must be hidden away forever and can never be cancelled. That is the strictest treatment possible. It makes no sense to say such an object is not forbidden at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Now. Opens a 'how could it be' argument.
Putting an object away permanently, through burial or hiding

phrases.english: Now, it requires burial,
phrases.notes: This refers to the known rule that a Jew's idol can never be cancelled, so it has to be put away for good.

phrases.english: and it would not become forbidden?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Argument from an accepted stricter rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A Jew's idol might not be forbidden at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since it needs גניזה, it is certainly forbidden.

steps.title: Maybe a Jew's idol is like a non-Jew's
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא grants that a Jew's idol is forbidden. Still, maybe it is forbidden only once worshipped, the same as a נכרי's.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say it is just like a non-Jew's idol!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a middle option. A Jew's idol is forbidden, but perhaps only after it is worshipped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 proved only that a Jew's idol is forbidden at some point. It did not prove when. Logic alone cannot tell us that it is forbidden immediately.

keyTerms.meaning: Like a נכרי's idol, meaning forbidden only once worshipped

phrases.english: But say it is like a non-Jew's!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to the conclusion of Step 6, left open by Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a Jew's idol is forbidden immediately
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being forbidden does not mean being forbidden immediately. It could follow the נכרי's timing.

steps.title: Proof from the golden calf: a sin from the moment it was made
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק calls the עגל 'your sin which you made'. This shows that a Jew's idol is a sin from the moment it is made, before any worship.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And your sin which you made, the calf.' From the time it was made, it already stood as a sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק about the עגל הזהב to prove that a Jew's idol is forbidden from the moment it is made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah calls the עגל a 'sin' connected to its making, not to its worship. So the sin starts with עשייה, the making of the idol. The next step challenges this proof, because it may only show that the person sinned. The final proof comes in step 14.

keyTerms.meaning: The calf, meaning the עגל הזהב
It stood as a sin, already counted as a sin

steps.confusionAlert: Logic alone (Steps 6-8) proved only that a Jew's idol is forbidden. The timing, 'immediately from making', is finally proven only in step 14, from 'תועבת ה׳'.

phrases.english: The verse says:
"And your sin, which you made,
the calf,"
phrases.notes: דברים 9:21

phrases.english: From the time of its making

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The עגל shows that making the idol is already a sin. Whether this makes the object forbidden is challenged in the next step.

steps.title: Maybe the verse only makes the person guilty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that 'your sin' only means the maker has sinned. The idol itself might still not be forbidden until it is worshipped.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe that only means the man is guilty of a sin, but the idol itself does not become forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from the עגל. It suggests the פסוק only tells us the person sinned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 used 'your sin which you made' to show a Jew's idol is a sin from the moment it is made. The challenge separates two things: the person being guilty, and the object being forbidden. Being a sinner does not automatically mean the object is אסור בהנאה.

keyTerms.meaning: To make the man stand guilty of sin

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the two separate ideas: the PERSON being guilty and the OBJECT being forbidden. The rest of this section is about this gap.

steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of 'your sin which you made' as proof that the idol is forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק may only say the person sinned. It does not show the object itself becomes forbidden.

steps.title: The curse starts from the time of making
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a פסוק saying 'Cursed is the man who makes an idol.' This shows the maker is cursed from the moment of making.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'Cursed is the man who makes a carved or molten image.' From the time of making, he is already under a curse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a stronger פסוק, ארור. It says the maker is cursed as soon as he makes the idol.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer tries to show that making the idol is already a serious event, strong enough to bring a curse. Notice that this still talks about the person, not the object. That opens the door for the next challenge.

steps.terutzMaskana: The maker is already cursed from the moment of making.

steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe that only means the man is cursed, but the idol itself does not become forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the same kind of challenge against the new פסוק. A curse on the man still does not prove the object is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words are almost the same as step 11, just with 'ארור' in place of 'sin.' The same gap remains: a punishment for the person is not a prohibition on the object.

steps.title: The idol itself is called an abomination
steps.stepSummary: The same פסוק calls the idol 'an abomination to ה׳.' That describes the object itself, so the object is forbidden from when it is made.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written: 'An abomination to ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points to words in the same פסוק, תועבת ה׳. These words describe the idol itself, not just the person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This finally closes the gap. 'Abomination' is a label on the object, so the idol itself is forbidden as soon as it is made, before any worship.
steps.whatToRemember: According to this side, a Jew's idol is forbidden from the moment it is made. The proof is that the פסוק calls the object itself תועבת ה׳.

phrases.english: "An abomination to ה׳" is written.
phrases.notes: This is the same פסוק, דברים 27:15.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 13 using further words of the same פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Closer reading of the same verse
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק might only punish the man.
steps.terutzMaskana: The idol itself is an abomination, so it is forbidden from when it is made.

steps.title: How does רבי עקיבא read this verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי עקיבא, who does not hold a Jew's idol is forbidden right away, explains 'abomination.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the other opinion. It asks how רבי עקיבא handles the word תועבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא holds the opposite: a Jew's idol is forbidden only after it is worshipped. Since the word 'abomination' seemed to prove the idol is forbidden right away, the גמרא asks how he explains it.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva?
phrases.notes: He's asking: how does רבי עקיבא explain 'abomination' if he holds a Jew's idol is not forbidden yet?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the other opinion deals with the proof in step 14.

steps.title: Abomination means something that leads to abomination
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא reads 'abomination' as something that will lead to abomination, not something that is already one.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is something that brings a person to abomination.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי עקיבא. The idol is called an abomination because it can lead to worship, not because it is already forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי עקיבא, the word looks ahead to what the idol will cause. A newly made idol is not yet forbidden. It becomes forbidden only once someone worships it.

phrases.english: An object that leads to abomination.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For רבי עקיבא, 'abomination' means an object that will lead to abomination. It is not yet forbidden in itself.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's source for a נכרי's idol
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רבי עקיבא learns that a נכרי's idol is forbidden immediately.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא, from where does he learn that a נכרי's idol is forbidden right away?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא asks for the other half of רבי עקיבא's view. It wants his source that a נכרי's idol is forbidden as soon as it is made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא says the reverse of the first side. A Jew's idol waits for worship, but a נכרי's idol is forbidden immediately. The גמרא wants a פסוק for this second half.

keyTerms.meaning: An idol belonging to a non-Jew
From where does he learn it?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva,
a gentile's idol,
that it is forbidden immediately, from where does he know it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁל נׇכְרִי דַּאֲסוּרָה מִיָּד מְנָא לֵיהּ?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from how רבי עקיבא reads 'abomination' to his source for the other half of his view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that a נכרי's idol is forbidden as soon as it is made.

steps.title: עולא: once carved it becomes a god
steps.stepSummary: עולא brings the פסוק 'the carved images of their gods you shall burn.' Once it is carved, it is already called a god.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: The verse says, 'The carved images of their gods you shall burn in fire.' From when he carves it, it becomes a god.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers with a פסוק about the idols of the nations. The פסוק calls them 'gods' already when they are carved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word פסילי, carved images, shows the idol is called a god from the moment it is carved. So a נכרי's idol is forbidden right away, even before worship.

keyTerms.meaning: The carved images of their gods

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא: a נכרי's idol is forbidden from when it is carved (פסילי אלהיהם). A Jew's idol is forbidden only after it is worshipped. He reads 'abomination' as something that leads to abomination, so that word does not prove otherwise. His actual source, 'ושם בסתר', comes in step 23.

phrases.english: Ulla said: The verse says:
"The carved images of their gods you shall burn in fire,"
phrases.notes: דברים 7:25

phrases.english: from when he carved it, it became a god.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא, אָמַר קְרָא: ״פְּסִילֵי אֱלֹהֵיהֶם תִּשְׂרְפוּן בָּאֵשׁ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From פסילי אלהיהם: as soon as the נכרי carves it, it is called a god and is forbidden.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל uses the verse for רב יוסף's teaching
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל does not use 'פסילי אלהיהם' the way עולא did. He needs it for רב יוסף's teaching that a נכרי can cancel his own idol.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other תנא, what does he do with this פסוק? He needs it for what רב יוסף taught: From where do we know that a נכרי can cancel his god? Because it says: 'The carved images of their gods you shall burn in fire.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks, in one word, how רבי ישמעאל uses the פסוק that רבי עקיבא used in step 18. It answers that he uses it for a different rule: a נכרי can cancel his idol.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each תנא can only use one פסוק for one rule. רבי ישמעאל reads 'פסילי' as coming from the word פסל, 'to make invalid.' So he learns that a נכרי can make his own god invalid, which is called ביטול.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one, meaning the other תנא in the argument
He needs it for something else
Carved images, which can also be heard as 'invalidated ones'

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the idea that a נכרי can cancel (בטל) his idol, which makes it permitted. The rest of this section builds on that idea.

phrases.english: And the other one? He needs that verse
phrases.notes: 'The other one' is רבי ישמעאל.

phrases.aramaic: לְכִדְתָנֵי רַב יוֹסֵף, דְּתָנֵי רַב יוֹסֵף:
phrases.english: for what Rav Yosef taught, as Rav Yosef taught:
From where do we know that a gentile can cancel his god?
As it says: 'The carved images of their gods you shall burn in fire.'
phrases.notes: דברים 7:25. רב יוסף hears 'פסילי' as 'their gods that they invalidate.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ, הַהוּא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְתָנֵי רַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the opposing תנא uses the פסוק that עולא used for רבי עקיבא, and answers it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How does רבי ישמעאל use 'פסילי אלהיהם'?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He uses it for רב יוסף's rule that a נכרי can cancel his idol.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא learns it from שמואל, who points out a contradiction
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא learns that a נכרי can cancel his idol from שמואל. שמואל points out that one פסוק seems to say two opposite things about the gold and silver on idols.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other תנא, he learns it from שמואל. שמואל pointed out a contradiction: It is written, 'Do not desire the silver and gold on them,' and it is also written, 'and take it for yourself.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רבי עקיבא learns רב יוסף's rule, since he already used 'פסילי' for something else. It answers that he learns it from שמואל, and this step lays out שמואל's contradiction. The next step gives שמואל's solution.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא used 'פסילי' in step 18 to show that a נכרי's idol is forbidden as soon as it is carved. So he needs another source for ביטול. שמואל notices that the פסוק forbids the gold, yet the words 'and take it for yourself' seem to allow it.

keyTerms.meaning: Points out a contradiction between two texts

phrases.english: And the other one? He learns it from Shmuel,
phrases.notes: Now 'the other one' is רבי עקיבא. He needs a source that a נכרי can cancel his idol.

phrases.english: for Shmuel pointed out a contradiction:
It is written: 'Do not desire the silver and gold on them,'
phrases.notes: דברים 7:25

phrases.english: and it is written: 'and take it for yourself.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ, נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִדִּשְׁמוּאֵל, דִּשְׁמוּאֵל רָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the question back on רבי עקיבא: where does he learn רב יוסף's rule?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where does רבי עקיבא learn that a נכרי can cancel his idol?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From שמואל's way of solving a contradiction in the פסוק.

steps.title: שמואל's solution: carved as a god versus canceled as a god
steps.stepSummary: If the נכרי carved it to be a god, the gold is forbidden. If he canceled it as a god, the gold may be taken.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does this work? If he carved it as a god, then 'do not desire' applies. If he canceled it from being a god, then 'take it for yourself' applies.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל solves the contradiction by saying the two parts of the פסוק describe two different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a wordplay here. 'פִּסְּלוֹ לאלוה' means he carved it into a god, so it is forbidden. 'פְּסָלוֹ מאלוה' means he canceled its status as a god, so it is permitted. This gives רבי עקיבא his source that ביטול works.

keyTerms.meaning: How can this be? (used to set up a solution)
He carved it to be a god
He canceled it from being a god

steps.whatToRemember: Both תנאים agree that a נכרי can cancel his idol. רבי ישמעאל learns it from 'פסילי' (רב יוסף), and רבי עקיבא learns it from שמואל's solution.

phrases.english: How can this be?
If he carved it as a god: 'do not desire,'
phrases.notes: The same letters, פסל, can mean 'carve' or 'cancel.' שמואל uses both meanings.

phrases.english: if he canceled it as a god: 'and take it for yourself.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Solves the contradiction raised by שמואל in step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each part of the פסוק describes a different situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seems to both forbid and allow the gold on idols.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is forbidden while it is a god and allowed once the נכרי cancels it.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's source that a Jew's idol is forbidden only once worshipped
steps.stepSummary: For רבי עקיבא, we have found why a נכרי's idol is forbidden right away. The גמרא asks where he learns that a Jew's idol is forbidden only after it is worshipped.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for רבי עקיבא: we found that a נכרי's idol is forbidden right away. From where do we learn that a Jew's idol is not forbidden until it is worshipped?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for רבי עקיבא's source for the other half of his view, about a Jew's idol. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא holds a split view. A נכרי's idol is forbidden as soon as it is made (step 18). A Jew's idol is forbidden only after it is worshipped. The second half still needs a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.english: And for Rabbi Akiva, we have found

phrases.aramaic: עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁל נׇכְרִי דַּאֲסוּרָה מִיָּד,
phrases.english: that a gentile's idol is forbidden right away,
but that a Jew's idol is not forbidden until it is worshipped, from where do we know?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, אַשְׁכְּחַן עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁל נׇכְרִי דַּאֲסוּרָה מִיָּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the נכרי's idol to the second half of רבי עקיבא's view, about a Jew's idol.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for רבי עקיבא's rule that a Jew's idol is forbidden only after it is worshipped.

steps.title: רב יהודה: 'and sets it up in secret'
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה brings the פסוק 'ושם בסתר': a Jew's idol is forbidden only once he does the hidden acts of worship to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: The פסוק says, 'and sets it up in secret.' That means it is not forbidden until he does to it the things done in secret.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question from step 22 with a פסוק about a Jew who makes an idol.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads 'in secret' as pointing to the acts of worship done to the idol. So making the idol alone is not enough. It becomes forbidden only once it is actually worshipped.

keyTerms.meaning: And sets it up in secret
Things done in secret, meaning the acts of worship

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: The verse says:
'and sets it up in secret,'
phrases.notes: דברים 27:15

phrases.english: meaning, not until he does to it the things done in secret.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר קְרָא: וְשָׂם בַּסָּתֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'ושם בסתר' teaches that a Jew's idol is forbidden only after the hidden acts of worship are done to it.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל uses the verse for רבי יצחק's teaching
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל needs 'ושם בסתר' for רבי יצחק's teaching that a Jew's idol must be hidden away (גניזה).
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other תנא? He needs that פסוק for what רבי יצחק said: From where do we know that a Jew's idol must be hidden away? Because it says, 'and sets it up in secret.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי ישמעאל uses 'ושם בסתר.' It answers that he uses it for רבי יצחק's rule that a Jew's idol must be put away in a hidden place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל holds that a Jew's idol is forbidden right away, so he cannot use this פסוק the way רבי עקיבא did. He reads 'in secret' as an instruction: the idol must be stored away (גניזה).

keyTerms.meaning: Must be stored away out of sight

steps.whatToRemember: The pattern here: each פסוק is used by one תנא for his own rule, and the other תנא uses it for a different teaching. For a Jew's idol: רבי עקיבא learns 'forbidden only once worshipped,' and רבי ישמעאל learns 'must be hidden away.'

phrases.english: And the other one? He needs that verse
phrases.notes: 'The other one' here is רבי ישמעאל.

phrases.english: for what Rabbi Yitzchak said, as Rabbi Yitzchak said:
From where do we know that a Jew's idol
must be hidden away?
As it says: 'and sets it up in secret.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ? הַהוּא מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ לְכִדְרַבִּי יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the opposing תנא uses רב יהודה's פסוק, and answers it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How does רבי ישמעאל use 'ושם בסתר'?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For רבי יצחק's rule that a Jew's idol must be hidden away (גניזה).

steps.title: רבי עקיבא learns גניזה from the אשרה next to the altar
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא used 'ושם בסתר' for something else, so he learns that a Jew's idol needs גניזה from רב חסדא: an אשרה is compared to the מזבח, and a מזבח needs גניזה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other (רבי עקיבא), where does he learn this? He learns it from what רב חסדא said in the name of רב: From where do we know that a Jew's idol must be hidden away? Because it says, 'Do not plant for yourself an אשרה, any tree, beside the altar.' Just as the altar must be hidden away, so too an אשרה must be hidden away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רבי עקיבא learns that a Jew's idol needs גניזה, since he used 'ושם בסתר' for a different lesson. It answers with a different פסוק, through רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 24, רבי ישמעאל learned גניזה from 'ושם בסתר'. רבי עקיבא already used that פסוק to teach that a Jew's idol becomes forbidden only once it is worshipped (step 23), so he needs another source. He uses the closeness of 'אשרה' and 'מזבח' in one פסוק: a broken or unfit מזבח is hidden away, so an אשרה is hidden away too.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (the other opinion), what does he do?
Hiding away or burying something so it is not used
A tree used for idol worship

phrases.english: And the other?
phrases.notes: This means רבי עקיבא. He used 'ושם בסתר' for something else, so where does he learn גניזה?

phrases.aramaic: נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִדְּרַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר רַב,
phrases.english: He derives it from what Rav Chisda said in the name of Rav,
as Rav Chisda said that Rav said:
From where do we know about a Jew's idol
that it must be hidden away?
As it says: "Do not plant for yourself an asherah,
any tree, beside the altar".
phrases.notes: דברים 16:21

phrases.english: Just as the altar must be hidden away,
so too an asherah must be hidden away.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ? נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִדְּרַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since רבי ישמעאל learned גניזה from 'ושם בסתר', the גמרא asks where רבי עקיבא learns it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where does רבי עקיבא learn that a Jew's idol needs גניזה?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From רב חסדא in the name of רב: 'לא תטע לך אשרה ... אצל מזבח'. The אשרה is compared to the מזבח, which needs גניזה.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל uses the אשרה פסוק for ריש לקיש's lesson about judges
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל does not learn גניזה from 'לא תטע', because he needs that פסוק for ריש לקיש: appointing an unfit judge is like planting an אשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other (רבי ישמעאל), what does he do with this פסוק? He needs it for what ריש לקיש said: Anyone who appoints an unfit judge is as if he plants an אשרה among the Jewish people. As it says, 'Judges and officers you shall appoint for yourself in all your gates,' and right next to it, 'Do not plant for yourself an אשרה, any tree.'
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא turns to רבי ישמעאל and asks what he does with the פסוק of 'לא תטע'. It answers that he needs it for a different lesson, taught by ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each תנא must have a use for both פסוקים. רבי ישמעאל uses the פסוק about the אשרה for a moral lesson: since it sits right next to the פסוק about appointing judges, appointing a bad judge is like planting an idol tree. So he cannot also use it to learn גניזה.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (for a different teaching)
Who is not fit or not worthy
And right next to it (in the תורה)

phrases.english: And the other?
phrases.notes: Now this means רבי ישמעאל. What does he do with the פסוק of 'לא תטע'?

phrases.english: He needs that verse for the teaching of Reish Lakish,
as Reish Lakish said:
Anyone who appoints a judge who is unfit
is as if he plants an asherah among the Jewish people,
as it says: "Judges and officers
you shall appoint for yourself in all your gates",
phrases.notes: דברים 16:18

phrases.english: and right next to it:
"Do not plant for yourself an asherah, any tree."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ? הָהוּא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After showing רבי עקיבא's use of 'לא תטע', the גמרא explains why רבי ישמעאל does not use it for גניזה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does רבי ישמעאל do with the פסוק 'לא תטע לך אשרה'?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He uses it for ריש לקיש's lesson that appointing an unfit judge is like planting an אשרה.
steps.whatToRemember: Both תנאים agree that a Jew's idol needs גניזה. רבי ישמעאל learns it from 'ושם בסתר'. רבי עקיבא learns it from 'לא תטע ... אצל מזבח', because he uses 'ושם בסתר' to teach that a Jew's idol is forbidden only once it is worshipped.

steps.title: An unfit judge where there are scholars is like an אשרה next to the altar
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי adds to ריש לקיש: appointing an unfit judge in a place with תלמידי חכמים is like planting the אשרה right beside the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: And in a place where there are תלמידי חכמים, it is as if he planted it next to the altar, as it says, 'beside the altar.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי builds on ריש לקיש's lesson and makes it stronger for one case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש used the first part of the פסוק, 'לא תטע לך אשרה'. רב אשי uses the end, 'אצל מזבח'. Passing over worthy scholars to appoint an unfit judge is even worse, like putting an idol tree right next to the holy altar.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
And in a place where there are Torah scholars,
it is as if he planted it next to the altar,
as it says: "beside the altar".

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: וּבִמְקוֹם תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds to ריש לקיש's teaching by using the rest of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Appointing an unfit judge where there are תלמידי חכמים is like planting an אשרה beside the מזבח.

steps.title: רב המנונא asks about welding a vessel for an idol
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא asks what the law is if someone welded a vessel for an idol.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא asked: If someone welded a vessel for an idol, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב המנונא asks a question, and the גמרא will first work out exactly what case he means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether welding a vessel for an idol counts as making it a forbidden item, or whether it stays permitted until it is actually used in worship. This sets up the clarification in the next step.

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna asked:
If one welded a vessel for an idol, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question, unrelated to the judge lesson.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does welding a vessel for an idol make the vessel forbidden?

steps.title: Whose idol is this about? It cannot be a נכרי's
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose idol רב המנונא means. It cannot be a נכרי's idol, because everyone agrees that idol accessories are forbidden only once they are used in worship.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose idol? If you say a נכרי's idol: according to both רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא, these are accessories of idol worship, and such accessories are not forbidden until they are used for worship!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא clarifies רב המנונא's question by testing one option, that it is about a נכרי's idol. It rejects that option, which prepares the real answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A vessel used for an idol is a משמשי עבודה זרה, an accessory, not the idol itself. Both תנאים agree that accessories are forbidden only after they are used. So for a נכרי's idol, the welded vessel is plainly permitted, and there would be nothing to ask.

keyTerms.meaning: Accessories, the items used to serve an idol
Until they are used in worship

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the idol itself with its accessories. רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא argue about when a נכרי's idol itself becomes forbidden, but both agree that the vessels that serve it are forbidden only after they are actually used.

phrases.english: Whose idol is this?
If you say it is a gentile's idol,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין לְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל וּבֵין לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
phrases.english: both according to Rabbi Yishmael and according to Rabbi Akiva
they are accessories of idol worship,
and accessories of idol worship are not forbidden
until they are used for worship!

steps.triggerLanguage: עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה דְּמַאן? אִילֵימָא עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה דְּנׇכְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies רב המנונא's question by ruling out the case of a נכרי's idol.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whose idol is רב המנונא's question about?
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the question is about a נכרי's idol
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Accessories of a נכרי's idol are forbidden only once used, according to both תנאים, so a welded vessel would clearly be permitted and there is no question.

steps.title: The question is about a Jew's idol
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רב המנונא must be asking about a Jew's idol.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is about a Jew's idol.
steps.whatsHappening: After ruling out a נכרי's idol, the גמרא decides that the question must be about an idol belonging to a Jew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the case of a נכרי's idol has a clear answer, the only open case is a Jew's idol. This sets up the next part of the discussion about how the two תנאים view a Jew's idol and the items connected to it.

keyTerms.meaning: An idol belonging to a Jew

phrases.english: Rather, it is about a Jew's idol.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the correct case after the first option was ruled out.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב המנונא's question is about a Jew's idol.

steps.title: Whose opinion is רב המנונא following?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא's view underlies רב המנונא's question about a Jew's idol.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whose opinion is he asking?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short setup question: which תנא's view is רב המנונא's question based on? The next steps will test the possible answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is an earlier מחלוקת about when a Jew's idol becomes forbidden. Before we can understand the question, we need to know which side of that מחלוקת it assumes.

phrases.english: According to whom?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that we know the question is about a Jew's idol, the גמרא asks which opinion about a Jew's idol it assumes.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's position on a Jew's idol the question follows.

steps.title: It cannot follow רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: Under רבי עקיבא, even the idol itself is forbidden only after it is worshipped. So obviously its accessories are too, and there would be nothing to ask.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it follows רבי עקיבא: the idol itself is not forbidden until it is worshipped. Do we even need to ask about its accessories?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries רבי עקיבא as the answer and rejects it. Under his view the question would be pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא holds that a Jew's idol becomes forbidden only once it is worshipped. If the main object needs worship, its accessories surely need to be used too. That leaves no real question.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a suggestion that is about to be tested)
Now (if this is true), introducing a 'how much more so' argument
Accessories: items used in serving the idol

phrases.english: If you say according to Rabbi Akiva,
now, the idol itself
is not forbidden until it is worshipped,
is there any question about its accessories?
phrases.notes: Of course the accessories also wait until they are used, so there is nothing to ask.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible answer to 'according to whom' and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rules out רבי עקיבא as the basis of the question.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Under רבי עקיבא the answer is obvious, so there would be no question at all.

steps.title: It follows רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: The question must follow רבי ישמעאל, who says a Jew's idol is forbidden immediately.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it follows רבי ישמעאל, who says: 'It is forbidden immediately.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles on רבי ישמעאל as the view behind רב המנונא's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי ישמעאל, a Jew's idol is forbidden the moment it is made. That leaves room for a real question about its accessories: are they also forbidden right away, or not?

phrases.english: Rather, according to Rabbi Yishmael,
who says: 'It is forbidden immediately.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי עקיבא is rejected, gives the other option as the answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The question follows רבי ישמעאל, who forbids a Jew's idol immediately.

steps.title: Laying out the two sides of the question
steps.stepSummary: Under רבי ישמעאל: do a Jew's idol accessories follow a נכרי's accessories (forbidden only once used), or the Jew's idol itself (forbidden immediately)?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law of the accessories? Do we learn them from other accessories? Then just as there they are forbidden only once used, here too. Or perhaps we learn them from the idol itself? Then just as it is forbidden immediately, its accessories are forbidden immediately too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now spells out what רב המנונא was really unsure about, using רבי ישמעאל's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two possible models. A נכרי's accessories become forbidden only once they are used in worship. A Jew's idol itself is forbidden immediately. The question is which of these two decides the law of a Jew's accessories.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps (the other side of a question)
From it (here: from the idol itself)

phrases.english: What about accessories?
Do we learn them from accessories?
phrases.notes: He means a נכרי's idol accessories, which become forbidden only once they are used.

phrases.english: Just as there, not until they are used in worship,
so too here, not until they are used in worship;
or perhaps he learns from it,
just as it is forbidden immediately,
so too its accessories are forbidden immediately?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Based on רבי ישמעאל's view, gives a first reading of what the question means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a Jew's idol accessories are compared to a נכרי's accessories or to the Jew's idol itself.

steps.title: Then why ask about welding?
steps.stepSummary: If that were the question, רב המנונא should have asked about making a vessel. Why did he pick welding?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does he ask specifically about someone who welded a vessel? Let him ask about someone who made one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reading in step 34. It does not fit the case רב המנונא actually chose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the issue were only accessories compared with the idol, any newly made vessel would raise it. Choosing welding, which means repairing a broken vessel, suggests the question is about something else.

phrases.english: Why specifically
does he ask about one who welded a vessel?
Let him ask about one who made one!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אִירְיָא דְּקָא מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ רִיתֵּךְ כְּלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading of the question given in step 34.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the question is about a Jew's accessories, compared either to a נכרי's accessories or to the idol itself.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reading would apply just as well to making a new vessel, so the word 'welded' would serve no purpose.

steps.title: The question is about an old status coming back
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא is really asking about טומאה ישנה. A vessel that had the impurity of עבודה זרה broke and was then welded back together: does its old impurity return?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא is asking because of old impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with a new reading. Welding matters because the question is whether an old status comes back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a vessel that was already used for an idol, and so became impure with the טומאה of עבודה זרה. It then broke, which purified it, and was welded together again. The question is whether that old טומאה returns, the way old טומאה returns to a remade metal vessel. That explains why he asked about welding and not about making a new vessel.

keyTerms.meaning: Old impurity: the impurity a vessel had before it broke

steps.confusionAlert: This is a new reading of the question, not an addition to step 34. The issue is no longer 'accessories compared with the idol' but 'does an old status come back after the vessel is repaired?'

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna
is asking because of old impurity,
phrases.notes: Think of a vessel that became impure from idol use, broke, and was then welded: does its old impurity come back?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הַמְנוּנָא מִשּׁוּם טוּמְאָה יְשָׁנָה קָמִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about welding by giving the question a different meaning.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines what the question is about.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The question was about a Jew's accessories, compared either to a נכרי's accessories or to the idol itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: The question is whether the impurity of עבודה זרה returns to a broken vessel once it is welded, like טומאה ישנה.

steps.title: The משנה about old impurity returning
steps.stepSummary: A משנה teaches that metal vessels that became טמא and then broke are טהור, but if they are remade into vessels, their old טומאה comes back.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: metal vessels, both flat ones and ones that hold things, become impure. If they broke, they became pure. If he remade them into vessels, they return to their old impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a משנה to show the idea behind רב המנונא's question: an old status can come back when a broken vessel is remade.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With metal vessels, breaking removes the טומאה, but remaking brings it back. רב המנונא wonders if the same is true of the impurity of a vessel used for an idol: once it became impure, broke, and was welded, does that impurity come back?

keyTerms.meaning: Flat vessels, with no space to hold anything
Vessels with a space that holds things

steps.whatToRemember: The reading of רב המנונא's question: a vessel that became impure from idol use breaks and is welded. Does its old impurity come back, just as old טומאה comes back to a remade metal vessel? Step 38 sharpens this further.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the word 'welded' was chosen on purpose. It links the laws of עבודה זרה to the idea from the laws of טומאה that an old status can return.

phrases.english: As we learned: metal vessels,
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in כלים 11:1.

phrases.english: their flat ones and their receptacles are impure,
if they broke, they became pure;
if he went back and made them into vessels,
they return to their old impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the idea of טומאה ישנה mentioned in step 36.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that an old status returns when a broken vessel is remade.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה כלים 11:1 about broken metal vessels.

steps.title: The real question: does rabbinic impurity come back too?
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא's question is stated exactly: does returning טומאה apply only to Torah-level impurity, or also to rabbinic impurity?
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he is asking: when impurity comes back to a remade vessel, is that only for Torah-level impurity and not rabbinic impurity? Or perhaps there is no difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now says exactly what רב המנונא wanted to know. The rule that טומאה returns was taught about Torah-level impurity, and he asks whether it also covers rabbinic impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה from step 37 shows that old טומאה returns when a broken vessel is remade. But the impurity of an idol's vessel is only מדרבנן. So the question is whether this 'coming back' rule reaches rabbinic impurity too.

keyTerms.meaning: or perhaps there is no difference

phrases.english: And this is what he is asking:
phrases.notes: "He" is רב המנונא, whose welding question we have been explaining.

phrases.english: When impurity comes back,
does that apply only to Torah-level impurity,
but not to rabbinic impurity?
Or perhaps there is no difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the משנה cited in step 37 to state רב המנונא's question exactly.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the rule that old טומאה returns apply to rabbinic impurity as well as Torah-level impurity?

steps.title: Why ask about idols? Ask about any rabbinic impurity
steps.stepSummary: If the question is about rabbinic impurity in general, why did רב המנונא choose עבודה זרה?
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him ask about other rabbinic impurities!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new explanation. If the question is really about rabbinic impurity, any rabbinic impurity would do, so why choose an idol's vessel?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are many kinds of rabbinic impurity. Picking עבודה זרה makes it seem that something about idols in particular matters to the question.

phrases.english: Let him ask about other rabbinic impurities!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reformulation in step 38.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that רב המנונא was asking about rabbinic impurity in general
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the question were about rabbinic impurity in general, mentioning עבודה זרה would be pointless.

steps.title: Two questions, one built on the other
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא asked two linked questions: does rabbinic impurity return at all, and if not, did the Rabbis treat idol impurity as strictly as Torah impurity?
steps.simpleTranslation: He is asking one question that grows out of another. Does rabbinic impurity come back or not? And if you say it does not come back, then for the impurity of עבודה זרה, because idolatry is so severe, did the Rabbis make it like Torah-level impurity, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב המנונא had two questions. The second only comes up if the first is answered 'no'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First question: does rabbinic impurity return when a vessel is remade? If it does not, a second question follows: since idolatry is so severe, perhaps the Rabbis gave idol impurity the full strength of Torah-level impurity, so it would return anyway. That second question is why עבודה זרה was mentioned.

keyTerms.meaning: they made it, treated it as

phrases.english: He is asking one question that grows out of another:
Does rabbinic impurity come back
or does it not come back?
And if you say it does not come back,
then the impurity of idol worship,
because of how severe idol worship is,
did the Rabbis make it like Torah-level impurity
or not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 39.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the question into two layered questions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The question was only about rabbinic impurity in general, so mentioning עבודה זרה seemed pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: The second question asks whether idol impurity has special strictness, which explains why עבודה זרה was chosen.

steps.title: The questions stay unresolved
steps.stepSummary: Both questions remain undecided.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends this discussion without an answer. Both of רב המנונא's questions stay open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source was found to decide whether rabbinic impurity returns, or whether idol impurity is treated like Torah impurity. The question about welding an idol's vessel is left as a doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: let it stand; the question stays unanswered

steps.whatToRemember: רב המנונא asked whether old rabbinic impurity returns to a remade vessel, and whether idol impurity is treated as strictly as Torah impurity. Both questions stay unresolved (תיקו).

phrases.english: Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the two questions laid out in step 40.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether rabbinic idol impurity returns to a remade vessel stays in doubt.

steps.title: Can ביטול purify food offered to an idol?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן asks רבי ינאי whether ביטול removes the impurity of food offered to an idol.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן asked רבי ינאי: what is the law for food offered to an idol? Does ביטול work to purify it from its impurity, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. רבי יוחנן asks whether ביטול, cancelling the idol status, also removes the impurity of food that was offered to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Things offered to an idol carry a rabbinic impurity. The question is whether ביטול removes only the forbidden status, or the impurity too, when the offering is food.

phrases.aramaic: בָּעֵי מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מֵרַבִּי יַנַּאי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan asked Rabbi Yannai:

phrases.aramaic: תִּקְרוֹבֶת עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁל אוֹכָלִים, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: Food offered to an idol, what is the law?
Does ביטול work for them
to purify them from impurity, or not?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מֵרַבִּי יַנַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question after the previous one ended in תיקו.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does ביטול remove the impurity of food offered to an idol?

steps.title: Why not ask about vessels?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן did not ask the same question about vessels.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him ask about vessels!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the choice of food. Vessels used for idols are impure too, so why not ask about them?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Vessels used for idols also carry this impurity. Limiting the question to food suggests there is a reason vessels are different.

phrases.english: Let him ask about vessels!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the scope of רבי יוחנן's question in step 42.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's choice of food as his case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Vessels are also impure from idol use, so the question could have been asked about them.

steps.title: Vessels can go in a מקוה; food cannot
steps.stepSummary: Vessels can become טהור in a מקוה, so ביטול surely removes their impurity. The doubt is only about food.
steps.simpleTranslation: He did not ask about vessels. Since they can become טהור in a מקוה, their impurity is also cancelled. He asked only about food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that vessels are an easy case. Their impurity is not permanent, because a מקוה can remove it, so ביטול can surely remove it too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Vessels can be purified in a מקוה, so ביטול clearly works on their impurity as well. Food cannot be purified in a מקוה, so its impurity might be permanent, and that is the real question.

keyTerms.meaning: becoming טהור by immersion in a מקוה

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think vessels are harder because they last longer. The point is the opposite: vessels can become טהור in a מקוה, so ביטול clearly works for them. Food is the real doubt.

phrases.english: He does not ask about vessels,
since they can become טהור in a מקוה,
their impurity is also cancelled by ביטול.
What he asks about is food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 43.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the other case is too obvious to ask about
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Vessels seemed to raise the same doubt as food.
steps.terutzMaskana: Vessels can be purified in a מקוה, so ביטול surely works for them. Only food, which a מקוה cannot purify, is in doubt.

steps.title: Why not ask about the idol itself?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if רבי יוחנן wanted to know whether ביטול removes the טומאה of food, he should have asked about the עבודה זרה itself, in a case where the idol is made of food.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him ask the question about the idol itself!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes again on how רבי יוחנן worded his question. It asks why he did not ask about the idol itself instead of only the food offered to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 44 explained that vessels were left out because they can become טהור in a מקוה, so his doubt was only about food. But an idol can also be made of food. So the גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן did not ask whether ביטול removes the טומאה of that kind of idol.

keyTerms.meaning: Then let him ask (the question about this case)
The idol itself (as opposed to things offered to it)
Cancelling an idol's status, done by an idolater

phrases.english: But let him ask about the idol itself!
phrases.notes: He means an idol that is itself made of food. That is the only case that would fit a question about food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 44 narrowed the question to food, the גמרא asks why it was not widened to an idol made of food.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of רבי יוחנן's question in step 42, which mentions only food offered to an idol.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If his doubt was about food and ביטול, an idol made of food is an equally good case. So why did he leave it out?

steps.title: He had no doubt about the idol itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its answer: רבי יוחנן did not ask about the idol itself because he had no doubt about it. The explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the idol itself he had no question.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to answer the challenge. It says the idol itself was never in doubt for רבי יוחנן. The reason comes at the start of the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is that the case was left out on purpose because it was clear to him, not because he forgot it. This sets up a contrast: the idol itself is a simple case, and only food offered to it (תקרובת) is a real question. The reason why the idol itself is simple has not been given yet.

keyTerms.meaning: He had no question about it; it was clear to him
Something offered to an idol, the case he did ask about

steps.confusionAlert: Don't stop here and think the answer is finished. The גמרא has only said the idol itself was clear to him. The reason why comes on the next amud.

phrases.aramaic: עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה גּוּפַהּ לָא מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: About the idol itself he had no question,

steps.triggerLanguage: עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה גּוּפַהּ לָא מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts to answer the challenge in step 45.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the omission: the left-out case was clear, so there was nothing to ask.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have thought רבי יוחנן should have asked about an idol made of food too.
steps.terutzMaskana: The idol itself was not in doubt for him, so he asked only about food offered to it. The reason is still to come.
